$comment: What a full run of e2e/configured/ must show, read by scripts/configured-verdict.mjs for BOTH workflows that run it: configured-suite.yml (local stack) and hosted-latency.yml (hosted staging). One file, so the two cannot drift. minTests is the number of tests that run: 82 ran on main on 2026-10-08 (configured-suite run 37795143698), plus the per-graphic replacement walk, the two community pack tests added with migration 0080, the two panel lease tests added with migration 0081, the two publish guard tests, the Home submit door test, the two control link and suspension guard tests added with migration 0088, the two sign-up tests (issue #794), the Take behind an Out walk (issue #914), the late commit notice walk (issue #917), the CLI set delivery walk in agent-access.spec.ts, its published entry path walk (npx from a clean home, a new account), and the two production link tests in deep-link-boot.spec.ts. It counts what runs in BOTH workflows, so a spec that runs on the local stack only is an allowed skip and stays out of the floor. Raise it in the change that adds a test or brings a skipped one back, and lower it deliberately in the one that removes a test. An entry in allowedSkips is coverage given up, so it needs its reason; take a file off in the change that makes it run again.

allowedSkips.connector-oauth.spec.ts: Runs on the local stack only: it registers OAuth clients, and hosted staging's Auth has no OAuth server until the owner enables it (docs/REMOTE_MCP_PLAN.md). Skips on hosted-latency.yml by design.
allowedSkips.connector-grants.spec.ts: Its consent walk runs on the local stack only (it registers OAuth clients, and hosted staging's Auth has no OAuth server until the owner enables it), and its 503 check runs on hosted staging only, where that is true. Each workflow skips the other half by design (docs/REMOTE_MCP_PLAN.md).
